problem: LLM-based embodied navigation is mostly simulated or relies on cloud/high-power hardware, and fixed landmark sets prevent using objects not known at deployment. Off-the-shelf tiny LLMs are not precise enough for low-level task decomposition.
motivation: Edge deployment (Jetson Nano, 4 GB) gives privacy, offline reliability and low latency dependence, but memory and power are tight. A robot needs to add newly seen objects as navigable landmarks so later instructions can reference them.
key_idea: Run a fine-tuned, quantized TinyLlama planner, a TensorRT YOLOv5n detector and ROS navigation all on a Jetson Nano, with detected objects continuously written into a growing knowledge base of navigable landmarks.
insight: Fine-tuning is essential: pre-trained TinyLlama scores 0/30 sub-tasks while the fine-tuned quantized model scores 27/30, close to cloud Cohere at 29/30. The growing KB ablation shows that with a fixed KB, manipulation prompts fail (0/4 or 1/4 sub-tasks), while the growing KB completes them 4/4. On-board planning costs latency (8-10 s vs 20 ms cloud) and power spikes (9.2 W vs ~6 W).
method: Path planning and execution: ROS1 with LiDAR SLAM on a pre-loaded map; services navigate_to_location, spin_service, grab_object, drop_object (grab/drop is simulated by a motion near the target).
Object detection and KB expansion: TensorRT YOLOv5n runs continuously, localizes objects with depth, filters them and stores pose/orientation into the KB as new landmarks.

Edge LLM planner: TinyLlama 1.1B fine-tuned with Unsloth on 20k samples (15k train/5k test; navigation and manipulation templates, rephrased with ChatGPT-4, varied KB headers), Q5_K_M quantized to 745 MB, run with llama.cpp, offloading layers between GPU and RAM/swap.
Plan execution: LLM outputs navigate(obj)/grab(obj)/drop() sub-tasks; if an object is not in the KB the task fails; otherwise navigate via KB coordinates or move the arm.
Dynamic process scheduling: the detector runs continuously while the LLM is loaded as a separate process and only decodes when a new prompt arrives, saving power and compute.

setting.training_data: 20,000 synthetic prompt-to-sub-task samples (15k train/5k test) built from templates with YOLO class names, rephrased with ChatGPT-4; 3 epochs, batch 5, lr 5e-5
setting.action_space: high-level sub-tasks navigate(landmark)/grab/drop executed via ROS navigation to waypoints on a Yahboom Transbot tracked robot
setting.privileged: pre-loaded map and initial landmark KB (home: 3 landmarks; office: 4 landmarks)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are sub-task correctness counts on 12 custom prompts in self-built real environments (e.g. 27/30 vs Cohere 29/30, pre-trained 0/30), latency and power measurements, not mappable to the canonical benchmarks.
results: The fine-tuned quantized TinyLlama achieves 27/30 correct sub-tasks versus 29/30 for cloud Cohere and 0/30 for the pre-trained model. The growing KB completes all object-based manipulation prompts (4/4) whereas a fixed KB gets 0/4 or 1/4. On-board latency is 8-10 s vs 20 ms for cloud, with peak power 9.2 W and swap ~50%.
limitations: Small, controlled indoor evaluation (handcrafted home/office, 12 prompts) with no standard benchmarks or baselines beyond Cohere
Physical grasping is simulated, the map and initial landmarks are pre-loaded, and the detector is closed-vocabulary YOLOv5n
High on-board latency (8-10 s) and memory pressure (92% RAM, 50% swap)
